summary: Iteration 4 testing — at-risk detection, reschedule/cancel-with-reason, real file upload, public shop-status page. Backend pytest: 11 passed, 1 failed (real bug in document download: UnicodeEncodeError on Content-Disposition because seeded shop names contain U+2014 em-dash). Frontend visual verification: dashboard renders 3 buttons per booked job (Start Driving / Dispatch to Contractor / Reschedule / Cancel — 4 actually, 'Start Driving' is the dispatch-to-self), 5 ⚠ AT RISK badges visible, 'At Risk' metric in summary strip, tomorrow strip rendered with 8 tomorrow-job mini-cards. Reschedule modal opens with shop+vehicle context, date picker (defaults today), reason quick-pick buttons + free-text, Confirm button. Cancel modal opens via same component with NO date picker (mode=cancel), reason controls present, Confirm hits POST /cancel. Public /scorecard/{token} page renders shop info, 4 stat cards (Jobs 35 / Completed 0 / Upcoming 29 / Total Spent $0), 'Book a new calibration' CTA, and full upcoming list. Invalid token shows 'Shop not found or link inactive'. ShopDetail testids 'shop-scorecard-link' and 'copy-scorecard' confirmed in source.

critical.issue: Returns 500 UnicodeEncodeError when filename contains non-latin-1 characters. Seeded shops are named 'Safelite — Gilbert', 'AutoGlassNow — Goodyear', 'Glass Doctor — Mesa' (U+2014 em-dash). spec_name pipeline preserves the em-dash and Content-Disposition header tries to encode as latin-1 and crashes. Fix: either ASCII-sanitize spec_name (replace non-ASCII with '_' or '-') before building the header, or use RFC 5987 filename*=UTF-8'' encoding (urllib.parse.quote).

issues: Card shows 4 action buttons (Start Driving, Dispatch to Contractor, Reschedule, Cancel) — spec said 3 (Dispatch/Reschedule/Cancel). 'Start Driving' is self-dispatch which is the owner's natural action, so this is intentional and not a defect, but worth confirming with PM.

action_items: FIX (HIGH): /api/documents/{id}/download crashes with UnicodeEncodeError when the spec filename contains an em-dash (or any non-latin-1 char) inherited from the shop name. Quick fix in server.py upload_document() spec_name line ~864 — strip/replace non-ASCII before storing, e.g.: spec_name = ''.join(c if ord(c) < 128 else '-' for c in spec_name)  OR  set the Content-Disposition header using RFC 5987: headers={'Content-Disposition': f"attachment; filename*=UTF-8''{urllib.parse.quote(doc['file_name'])}"}
OPTIONAL: server.py is now 1264 lines — splitting into routers (jobs/docs/public/contractors) is overdue.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py upload_document: stores entire base64 payload in MongoDB document — fine for MVP but a 10 MB blob ≈ 13.3 MB base64 + BSON overhead which approaches the 16 MB BSON document limit. Recommend GridFS or S3 before production.
server.py download_document: no Content-Disposition filename sanitization for unicode (root cause of the 500 above).
annotate_at_risk: only considers status booked/driving/on_site — 'dispatched_to_contractor' jobs that are past start are never flagged. If a contractor accepts late, the owner has no risk visibility.

reschedule_job: does not validate the new slot against zone-window or check for overlap with existing jobs — could accidentally double-book or schedule outside zone hours. Reschedule UI uses /public/availability which does enforce this, but the API itself is permissive.
public/shop-status: 'upcoming' filter includes 'dispatched_to_contractor' which is correct, but 'booking_link' field in response duplicates 'booking_link_token' — minor.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on testid presence + visual confirmation of reschedule modal, cancel modal, at-risk badges, At Risk metric, tomorrow strip, scorecard public page (valid + invalid token), shop detail scorecard URL block

rca of the issue: Document download 500: server.py line ~903 builds Content-Disposition with filename containing U+2014 (em-dash) which Starlette serializes as latin-1 → UnicodeEncodeError. Reproduction: upload any file to a job whose shop name has an em-dash (all 3 seeded shops do) → GET /api/documents/{id}/download → 500. Mitigation A (simple): sanitize spec_name in upload_document() to ASCII-only. Mitigation B (correct): use RFC 5987 in Content-Disposition: filename*=UTF-8''<percent-encoded>. Mitigation B preserves the original filename; Mitigation A loses fidelity but is one line.
